sections.title: PROPOSED FIX
sections.body:
surface fill-vs-plan geometry slippage in /api/stats/by-setup so plannedRr stops being write-only
File: server/index.js — the `app.get("/api/stats/by-setup")` handler at 3939, accumulator init at 3971, per-trade fold at 3983-3986, emit at 3993-3997.
Change: alongside the existing totalRR/rrTrades pair, accumulate `totalPlannedRr`/`plannedRrTrades` from `t.plannedRr` (Number.isFinite guard, same shape as the impliedRR guard at 3983), and count `filledBelowMinRr` = rows where `impliedRR < 1.5` while `plannedRr >= 1.5`. Emit `avgPlannedRr`, `avgRR`, `avgRealizedR` side by side plus `filledBelowMinRr`. Payload-only; touches no gate, no threshold, no order path.
Evidence: the field is written on every fill at 4318 with an explicit comment about keeping slip visible, and grep proves no reader exists. On today's 7 rows it immediately fires once — SP500 ticket 1798862395, planned 2.0, filled 1.18, MIN_RR 1.5 — and would have been silent on the five rows where plan and fill agree within 0.05.
Cost in samples: zero. This blocks nothing and fires nothing; it converts every fill the system already takes into an additional measurement of how far execution moves the geometry the gate approved. That is the constraint the brief names.
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: if `filledBelowMinRr` stays at 0 across the next ~15 fills, the 1.18 row is a one-off from a stale signal cache rather than a systematic bridge-fill drift, and the right fix is upstream in the bridge's price handoff instead. If it fires repeatedly, the next question is whether MIN_RR should be re-checked against fill prices — but that question needs the measurement first, and deliberately not before, since re-checking at fill would kill trades and cost samples.
[exit 0]

rather than silently attributing it to whatever setup the live signal cache
currently holds. Evidence: journal.json ticket 1682651222 tagged
BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH despite hermes.js:125 and index.js:1140 both defining that
setup as non-entry/WAIT - this same mislabeling corrupts updateLearning()
(index.js:3216) and the negative-expectancy bench check in hermes.js:132,
both of which key off trade.setup.
